title: He opened their understanding (Luke 24:44–49)
hookLine: the whole of the scriptures is about him

lines: SOME BOOKS NEED A SECOND READ.
cards: Some books only make sense on the second read. The detective novel whose last chapter sends you back to page one, and suddenly every small detail was a clue. The film you rewatch knowing the twist.
The disciples have had the scriptures all their lives: Moses, the prophets, the psalms, read aloud every Sabbath since they were children. They know the words.
But tonight, still in that room, with the fish bones on the table, the risen Jesus gives them the last chapter, and sends them back to page one.

teach.b: He reminds them of what he told them while he was still with them: everything written about him in the law of Moses, in the prophets, and in the psalms had to be fulfilled.
Those are the three parts of the scriptures as people in his time often named them: the whole book.
Then the sentence that gives today its name: "Then he opened their understanding, that they might understand the scriptures." Opened. It's the same Greek verb Luke has used all chapter.
On the road, the scriptures were opened to the two from Emmaus. At the table, their eyes were opened. Now, minds.
Reading the Bible well isn't only a matter of effort. Something has to be opened, and the risen Christ is the one who opens it.
He sums it up: the Christ should suffer and rise again the third day, and repentance and forgiveness of sins should be preached in his name to all nations, beginning at Jerusalem. You are witnesses.
Then: stay in the city until you are clothed with power from on high, a promise Luke keeps in his second book, Acts, at Pentecost. The Catholic Church still reads the scriptures this way.

teach.h: THE NEW HIDDEN IN THE OLD.
teach.b: The Second Vatican Council, in Dei Verbum, says the two Testaments belong together, and quotes an old line from Saint Augustine: the New is hidden in the Old, and the Old is made plain in the New.
Catholics also say the Old Testament keeps its own lasting worth, and the Jewish people read these same books in their own living tradition. Both are true at once.

how: Catholics hear the scriptures at Mass in a pattern that pairs an Old Testament reading with the Gospel, and the Church teaches, in Dei Verbum, that the two Testaments are read in the light of each other.

games.q: what does “he opened their understanding” mean?
o: Jesus explaining his parables to the crowds by the lake
the risen Jesus showing how the scriptures speak of him
the Spirit coming on the disciples at Pentecost

games.q: the whole book — tap the pairs.
p: the law, the prophets, the psalms

s: the disciples had never read the scriptures
they knew them all their lives. what was opened was their understanding.
Luke uses the same verb, opened, again and again in this chapter
the scriptures opened, eyes opened, and now understanding opened.
Dei Verbum says the New Testament is hidden in the Old
it quotes Augustine: the New hidden in the Old, the Old made plain in the New.

games.q: you're the risen Christ with your friends for one evening. they've touched you and watched you eat. what do you give them next?
o: a new book to replace the old one.
a way to read the scriptures they already have.
a list of rules for the new community.
games.why: he opened their understanding, that they might understand the scriptures, the law, the prophets and the psalms, as speaking of him.

practice: Bring to mind a line of scripture that has puzzled you, bothered you, or just slid past, maybe one from this week: green wood and dry, forgive them, the idle tales. Turn it over slowly without trying to solve it.
If you pray, ask simply to understand it; if you don't, stay curious with it, the way you'd sit with a hard question from a friend.

wordCard.voice: He opened their understanding. The risen Jesus showing his disciples that the law, the prophets and the psalms speak of him. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: he opened up, the verb Luke uses for the scriptures, the eyes and the mind in chapter 24.

carryVoice: Your line: opened. And that's week seventy: green wood, Father, the centurion, idle tales, Emmaus, broiled fish, and opened.

sources.q: Then he opened their understanding, that they might understand the scriptures.
